title: JEE Main 2026 (April 2nd, Shift 2) - Chemistry - Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure
subject: Chemistry

questions.q:
$\text{SF}_4$ is isostructural with:
A. $\text{BrF}_4^-$
B. $\text{CH}_4$
C. $\text{IF}_4^+$
D. $\text{XeF}_4$
E. $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explain:
To find isostructural species, we determine the hybridization and shape using VSEPR theory.
$\text{SF}_4$: Central S has 6 valence $e^-$, forming 4 bonds $\rightarrow$ $1$ lone pair. It has 5 electron pairs ($sp^3d$), shape is see-saw.
A. $\text{BrF}_4^-$: Br has $7+1=8$ valence $e^-$, forming 4 bonds $\rightarrow$ $2$ lone pairs. Shape is square planar.
B. $\text{CH}_4$: C has 4 valence $e^-$, forming 4 bonds $\rightarrow$ $0$ lone pairs. Shape is tetrahedral.
C. $\text{IF}_4^+$: I has $7-1=6$ valence $e^-$, forming 4 bonds $\rightarrow$ $1$ lone pair. Shape is see-saw.
D. $\text{XeF}_4$: Xe has 8 valence $e^-$, forming 4 bonds $\rightarrow$ $2$ lone pairs. Shape is square planar.
E. $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$: Xe has 8 valence $e^-$, 4 $e^-$ used for 2 O (double bonds), 2 $e^-$ for 2 F (single bonds). Total $4$ bonding regions, leaving $1$ lone pair. Shape is see-saw.
Hence, $\text{IF}_4^+$ and $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$ are isostructural with $\text{SF}_4$.
